label: lad-da6de
summary: A dense ReLU network that scores a Connect-4 position for x, the player to move. In effect it rates central control: its mean predicted chance of an x win climbs from 23% in the lowest band to 97% in the highest band of the classic square-value score (each piece weighted by the number of lines of four through its square, x plus, o minus), so x pieces in the centre columns raise it and x pieces on the outer bottom-row squares lower it. The ReLU thresholds add position-specific corrections on top (straightening every unit together drops training AUC from 0.948 to 0.854), and where those corrections overrule the square-value score the observed outcomes side with the model. The output is a sigmoid vote of the hidden units for and against an x win.

resisted: The individual hidden units resisted: none is a nameable Connect-4 feature (straightening any one unit alone costs at most 0.020 of training AUC), and the position-specific corrections were not traced to a rule such as a particular threat; a constructed swap that hands o a centre square and x a corner square raised x's predicted win from 80% to 99% against the square-value score. The hidden layer also could not be divided into smaller annotated parts: the layer is dense, each input square fans out to more units than the split operation can copy a node into, so the whole hidden layer is one leaf.

recheck_notes: No mismatch and no needs_review item. The unchecked free-text sentences carry no numbers (structure, wording, and the domain reading backed by the referenced queries in neighbouring sentences).
tool_bugs: split_node cannot split a node with more than 26 outgoing edges ('Too many splits, ran out of letters'), and validate_operation reports such a split as valid; every input here feeds 32 hidden units, so no input can be split and the hidden layer cannot be divided into several leaves with full structural coverage. The text lint flags 'zero' in the phrase naming the ablation mode (to='zero'); reworded rather than proved, since it is not a count.

refuted_and_fixed: board_detectors: 'a centre square handed to o lowers x's predicted win' was contradicted by the row-1309 swap; the hypothesis was written as a population-level reading with that counterexample stated

leaves.name: board_detectors
leaves.why: On real positions the layer's output tracks the classic square-value (centre-control) score band by band, but single units are not nameable features and some position-specific corrections, which the outcomes support, were not traced to a rule.

overall_function: The network rates a Connect-4 position for x by central control: x pieces in the centre columns (above all column d) raise the predicted chance of an x win and o pieces there lower it, while pieces on the outer bottom-row squares count the other way, much like the classic count of lines of four through each square. The hidden layer is dense, so there is no single input gate; the ReLU units act together as a population, adding position-specific corrections on top of that centre-control score, and those corrections move the prediction substantially in some positions (for example a corner piece can swing it from a likely win to a likely loss). The output is a sigmoid of a vote between units that push for an x win and units that push against it. The dense layer reads the whole board; the rarely filled top rows can only act in the few positions that reach them.
stuck: Operations: inputs with 32 outgoing edges cannot be split (26-letter limit), so the dense hidden layer had to be one leaf; a finer hierarchy (e.g. pro-win and anti-win unit groups as separate leaves) was impossible without losing structural coverage. Leaf meaning: the units are distributed and not individually nameable; the nonlinear corrections were described by their effect and their agreement with outcomes, not by a rule. Tools: no query computes a correlation or a population-average single-square flip, so the centre-control reading is shown by subgroup bands and constructed swaps.
